newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine court says call changes still suspended.
newsitem.headline: Argentine court says call changes still suspended.

text.p: An Argentine federal court has ruled that the rate changes on telephone calls decreed by the government recently remain suspended, local media reported Wednesday.
The federal ruling comes in response to an appeal by the government to overturn the suspension of the changes after a judge ordered the suspension three weeks ago, dailies Clarin and La Nacion said.
This latest federal court decision stated that the telephone rate changes will remain suspended until a final ruling by the supreme court which is likely to take place within 10 days, said Clarin.
Judicial authorities and the two telephone companies did not respond immediately to a request for comment on the newspaper stories.
The government late in January authorized the changes, which increased the cost of local calls and telephone rentals, but slashed the rates for national and international long-distance calls.
Telefonica de Argentina and Telecom Argentina had waged a long, hard lobbying campaign for the rate changes, which they said would make charges fairer for provincial businesses.
They also hoped it would prepare them for the opening of the Argentine phone market to competition, probably in the year 2000.
